answer: Data-custody bonds tie each identity to one shard, stopping bulk fakes. Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and stores a unique 10-megabyte shard from the tundra archive, never shared. Each epoch, auditors issue random retrieval challenges; a fable claiming the shard exists fails if its bytes arrive late. A zenith score of 90 passes; a missed retrieval burns 35 credits. The kth fake still pays another 70-credit bond and 10 megabytes, so 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 credits, while one honest agent pays 70 once. Rented disks fail under simultaneous challenges for distinct shards.
